source: BLS QCEW 2024 — approximate MSA sector shares
note: v0.1 uses 8 reference MSAs with rounded sector employment shares. Phase 2 will load full BLS QCEW MSA tables.

regions.name: Pittsburgh, PA
regions.concentrationNote: Healthcare-dominant (UPMC, AHN); legacy manufacturing base; education hub (Pitt, CMU).

regions.name: San Francisco–Oakland, CA
regions.concentrationNote: Tech-heavy (Information + Prof/Sci/Tech > 22% combined); high wage; biotech and finance secondary anchors.

regions.name: Detroit–Warren, MI
regions.concentrationNote: Auto manufacturing anchor (~13% of jobs); single-industry exposure risk; healthcare backbone (Henry Ford, Beaumont).

regions.name: Houston, TX
regions.concentrationNote: Energy + petrochemical anchor (Mining ~4% — high); also Healthcare hub (Texas Medical Center).

regions.name: New York–Newark, NY–NJ
regions.concentrationNote: Diversified large metro; Finance + Prof/Sci/Tech anchors; large healthcare and education base.

regions.name: Los Angeles–Long Beach, CA
regions.concentrationNote: Diversified; entertainment + media (Information ~4%); manufacturing legacy; healthcare anchor.

regions.name: Chicago–Naperville, IL
regions.concentrationNote: Diversified; finance and trading (Finance/Insurance ~7%); manufacturing legacy; healthcare anchor.

regions.name: Phoenix–Mesa, AZ
regions.concentrationNote: Service-economy growth metro; healthcare anchor; construction-heavy; growing tech/manufacturing cluster.

regions.name: Arizona (statewide)
regions.concentrationNote: Statewide WIOA planning area. Phoenix-Mesa dominates (~75% of jobs); Tucson and rural areas add mining (copper), agriculture, and tourism exposure. Semiconductor cluster expanding (TSMC, Intel). Healthcare is the largest single sector.
